thread:
marta: Heads up — noticed a ~22% drop in prefix/prompt prefetch hit-rate on the canary after the kernel-selection change. p99 token latency increased ~30ms for some routes. repro + short traces below.

jay: ugh. which canary and which change exactly? link to the dashboard pls.

marta: canary: eu-west-dedicated-2. change: kernel-picker now spreads sub-batches across kernels to improve GPU utilization. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/AXYz/prefetch-hitrate?orgId=1&var-env=canary

marta: quick query we used:
```
sum(rate(prefetch_cache_hits_total{env="canary"}[$__range])) by (model,route,kernel)
/ sum(rate(prefetch_cache_lookups_total{env="canary"}[$__range])) by (model,route,kernel)
```

priya: I profiled the handoff path. when batch split happens we do an extra copy + per-kernel header that modifies the serialized prompt framing. basically the same prompt string is ending up with slightly different prepended metadata, which changes the cache key hash. see flamegraph (short): `/prof/trace/2026/3659999987`

liam: so keys are content-equal but not byte-equal after the kernel header injection? can we normalize before hashing?

marta: exactly. examples:
```
# old serialized prefix (hit)
{"route":"search","seq": [0,1,2],"prefix":"user: hi"}
# new after kernel split (miss)
{"route":"search","kernel":"k1","seq": [0,1,2],"prefix":"user: hi"}
```
hashes differ. current keying uses the full serialized payload + sequence boundary marker.

jay: nasty. two short-term options: 1) normalize out transient kernel field from the cache-key path, or 2) enforce kernel affinity for a request series so it never splits. both have tradeoffs.

priya: normalization seems safest for correctness. but watch out for legitimate kernel-dependent rewrites (e.g., quantization flags). we should whitelist which fields are safe to drop.

marta: agreed. I ran a quick experiment patching the key derivation to drop `kernel` and `hand_off_id` fields and re-ran synthetic workload: hit-rate recovered ~19% (still short of baseline, likely other formatting diffs). p99 dropped back down ~25ms.

infra-bot: deploy canary finished: deploy/2026-03-12-kerpick-v2 -> eu-west-dedicated-2 :white_check_mark:

liam: can we add a dashboard panel that compares "effective tokens saved" per-customer between the two kernel strategies? metrics we want: prefetched_tokens_saved_total, prefetch_hitrate, requests_split_by_kernel_ratio.

priya: SQL I used to compute per-customer token savings delta:
```
select customer_id,
  sum(prefetched_tokens_saved) filter (where env='canary') as saved_canary,
  sum(prefetched_tokens_saved) filter (where env='baseline') as saved_baseline,
  (saved_baseline - saved_canary) as delta
from prefetched_token_events
where ts between now() - interval '24 hours' and now()
group by customer_id
order by delta desc
limit 50;
```

marta: added the panel and a temporary synthetic cohort to the dashboard. also created an alert rule: if global prefetch hit-rate drops >10% for 10m trigger P1. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/+/pr/4821 (key-normalizer + unit tests).

jay: nice. can you add a canary A/B where 50% go kernel-affinity path, 50% go normalized-key path so we can measure production tradeoffs? include tail-latency and GPU utilization.

marta: yes. I'll spin up the split and tag experiments. quick checklist:
- [ ] final whitelist of fields safe to drop from cache key (priya + marta)
- [ ] A/B canary split (marta)
- [ ] per-customer token-saved diff panel (priya)
- [ ] follow-up perf profile after split (liam)

priya: putting the field whitelist doc here: https://docs.internal/srv/prefetch-key-whitelist.md — start with `kernel`, `hand_off_id`, `trace_id` but keep `model_version`, `prompt_config`.

liam: any chance the batching heuristic itself is increasing inter-request reordering causing cache warmup regressions? we should also look at sequence-boundary detection.

marta: good call. next profiling run will include sequence boundary counts per-route. posting updates in this thread as we run the A/B. thanks all :)
